To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the photochemistry of aliphatic cis azo compounds is dominated by the thermal properties of the parent molecule.

the photochemical decomposition of aliphatic cis azo compounds is a highly stereospecific process and that the barrier to singlet state decomposition can be lowered by raising the temperature, by increasing the strain of the azoalkene system, and by making the azobicycloalkane system more labile therm ally.

the photochemical decomposition of bicyclic and bridgehead vinyl substituted diazacycloalkanes is a useful method of ring opening, and that the photochemistry of cis l—aza-bicyclo[2,2,1]heptane is an example of a new type of photochemistry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the photochemical decomposition of azo compounds and the photochemical isomerization of azoalkenes.
the photochemistry of azoalkanes, with the photochemical decomposition of azoalkenes, and with the photochemistry and thermal decomposition of bicyclic diazo compounds.
the synthesis and properties of a variety of unusual azo compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photochemical properties of azoalkanes are determined by the thermally determined properties of the azoalkanes.
photochemical decomposition of azoalkanes is not a general reaction.
the azo group in an alkane is a thermally and photochemically labile group which is subject to a wide variety of reactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
photochemical azo group loss is a general property of azoalkanes and azoalkenes.
the azoalkanes are not particularly reactive photochemically and that they are more reactive thermally than they are photochemically.
the photochemical behavior of azo compounds is strongly influenced by the presence of a strained ring in the molecule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photochemical decomposition of azoalkanes can be controlled by judicious choice of substituents.
the azo group in an azoalkane can be used to control the course of photochemical decomposition reactions.
the azo group can be incorporated into strained systems without destroying their strain.
